spec: DESIGN.md — Vocabulary; issue #784 (D7–D9, D11, D14, D27); vectors/README.md — The platform-table family
description: Pairs in, the platform table's translation out, in the projection both families assert: per pair and for the intersection, every source's keys with their relation; none, unknown and conflict as stated values.

vectors.name: a-romm-slug-covers-three-es-de-systems
vectors.rationale: RomM folds the folders genesis, megadrive and megadrivejp into its genesis slug (platform_aliases.py), so the slug is broader than each ES-DE system: ES-DE answers three keys, each narrowMatch — a finer vocabulary, never uncertainty (#784 D8). EmuDeck's genesiswide folder is a content subset of ES-DE's genesis, so it answers as a part of it: narrowMatch (#784 D37).

vectors.name: a-bare-folder-is-the-union-of-every-folder-vocabulary
vectors.rationale: A bare folder name means what every folder vocabulary means by it (#784 D14): ES-DE's megadrive is one system, Batocera's megadrive covers Genesis and the Japanese Mega Drive too (its platform list), so the folder alone names three ES-DE systems. EmuDeck's genesiswide, a content subset of ES-DE's genesis, answers as a part of it: narrowMatch (#784 D37).

vectors.name: a-second-pair-narrows-the-folder-to-one-system
vectors.rationale: Only another pair narrows a bare folder (#784 D9, D14): with ES-DE's megadrive beside it the intersection is the one system.

vectors.name: romms-arcade-slug-covers-fourteen-rows
vectors.rationale: RomM 5.4.1 folds thirteen folders into its arcade slug, which with the slug's own arcade folder reach fourteen rows: twelve ES-DE systems and Batocera's namco22 and namco2x6, every one of them narrower than the slug.

vectors.name: two-systems-share-nothing-and-are-a-conflict
vectors.rationale: The Super Game Boy and the Game Boy Color are two systems: the pairs intersect in nothing, and the answer names both pairs as the conflict — atlas picks neither (#784 D9).

vectors.name: a-romm-only-system-has-no-key-anywhere-else
vectors.rationale: The Altair 8800 is a RomM slug no frontend, distribution, core or registry in the table names: every source but RomM's own two columns (its slug and its folder of that spelling) answers none, which is a definite answer (#784 D3).

vectors.name: a-source-the-table-does-not-hold-is-unknown
vectors.rationale: MobyGames is not a source of the table (#784 D21): the pair is unknown, stated with platform-source-unknown, which names the asked source and the table's sources (#784 D31), never guessed.

vectors.name: a-stated-source-version-the-table-does-not-hold-is-a-caveat
vectors.rationale: The client says its key comes from RomM 5.3.0; the table holds RomM at 5.4.1, so the answer is the 5.4.1 meaning with the platform-source-version-differs caveat (#784 D11).

vectors.name: rocknix-pc-is-related-to-dos
vectors.rationale: ROCKNIX's pc folder is its DOS system, not ES-DE's IBM PC system: a reviewed override relates it to ES-DE's dos (relatedMatch), so a client is told the overlap, not an identity.

vectors.name: a-combined-romm-slug-is-broader-than-two-batocera-keys
vectors.rationale: RomM's combined slug for the Sharp MZ-80B/2000/2500 line covers Batocera's mz2000 and mz2500: each Batocera key is narrower than the slug.

vectors.name: a-renamed-batocera-key-is-the-es-de-system
vectors.rationale: Batocera's jaguar is ES-DE's atarijaguar under another spelling (a reviewed rename); KNULLI's jaguar follows it onto the same row.

vectors.name: an-igdb-id-reaches-both-es-de-systems-of-its-console
vectors.rationale: IGDB 19 is RomM's IGDB record for the Super Nintendo Entertainment System. RomM's snes slug reaches ES-DE's snes alone (and Batocera's snes-msu1, which RomM folds into it); a reviewed override places the record on ES-DE's snesna as well, the same console under a second ES-DE system with the same full name. So ES-DE's snes and snesna are each narrower than 19, and so is RomM's own snes slug: the slug covers snes, the record covers snes and snesna. ES-DE's sfc is not reached: the Super Famicom is IGDB's record 58. EmuDeck's sneshd, a content subset of ES-DE's snes, answers as a part of it: narrowMatch (#784 D37).

vectors.name: the-cd32s-ids-stay-on-the-cd32
vectors.rationale: IGDB 114 is RomM's IGDB record for the Amiga CD32. RomM resolves the folder amigacdtv to its CD32 slug, so the slug covers ES-DE's cdtv as well; ES-DE's scraper map gives the CDTV its own ScreenScraper id, and a reviewed override keeps the CD32's ids on ES-DE's amigacd32 alone. RomM's own slug still covers both, as RomM states it.

vectors.name: the-game-boy-colors-ids-stay-off-the-super-game-boy
vectors.rationale: ScreenScraper 10 is the Game Boy Color in ES-DE's scraper map and RomM's list. RomM resolves the folders sgb and sgb-msu1 to its gbc slug, which carried the id onto the Super Game Boy; ES-DE's map gives the Super Game Boy its own id 127, and a reviewed override keeps 10 on ES-DE's gbc and Batocera's two-player Game Boy Color system.

vectors.name: a-folder-only-rocknix-spells-is-still-a-folder
vectors.rationale: A bare folder name is matched against every folder vocabulary, ROCKNIX's included: pico-8 is ROCKNIX's spelling alone, and it still answers PICO-8 in every source that has a key for it.

vectors.name: a-folder-only-emudeck-spells-is-still-a-folder
vectors.rationale: A bare folder name is matched against every folder vocabulary, EmuDeck's included: sneshd is EmuDeck's spelling alone, a folder for one part of the SNES's games, and it answers through EmuDeck's key. As a content subset of ES-DE's snes it answers as a part of that system (#784 D37): every source's SNES key is broadMatch, a coarser key, while sneshd stays exact to itself.

vectors.name: a-key-is-compared-exactly-as-its-source-spells-it
vectors.rationale: Keys compare exactly as their source spells them, case included (#784 D34): IGDB's slug is snes, so SNES is unknown and stated with platform-unmapped, while snes beside it is known — no source's keys are case-folded.

vectors.name: a-version-on-a-bare-folder-is-not-applied
vectors.rationale: A bare folder name is matched against every folder vocabulary, so a version names no single source: it is not applied, the union stands, and platform-version-unapplied names the version (#784 D32). A client that wants it applied asks the folder vocabulary by name.

vectors.name: a-key-the-table-excludes-states-its-reason
vectors.rationale: RomM has the slug bubble, and the table places it on no row on purpose: no included source states what it is. The pair is unknown with platform-excluded and the reason platform_excluded.json records (#784 D35), not platform-unmapped, which is for a key the source does not have.

data.reason: no included source states what this is (looked in: RomM's IGDB, ScreenScraper and LaunchBox tables; only its MobyGames table names it, moby_handler.py:428, and MobyGames is not shipped)

vectors.name: a-bare-folder-the-table-excludes-states-its-reason
vectors.rationale: bubble is a RomM folder the table excludes with its slug, and no other folder vocabulary spells it: the bare folder is unknown with platform-excluded and that folder vocabulary's recorded reason (#784 D14, D35).

data.reason: no included source states what this is (the folder of the slug's own spelling resolves to romm/bubble, excluded for the same reason)

vectors.name: a-part-key-makes-the-shared-system-a-part
vectors.rationale: libretro's Wii (Digital) database covers only part of the Wii, so the two pairs share that part of the system (#784 D36): Wii (Digital) is exactMatch, the part being its own; every key covering the whole Wii, ES-DE's asked wii included, is broadMatch over it; RetroDECK's primehack and EmuDeck's primehacks, another part of the Wii (D37), are relatedMatch — the table cannot know whether two parts overlap.

vectors.name: a-part-and-its-system-intersect-on-the-part
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck's sneshd is a content subset of ES-DE's snes, so the two pairs agree on that part rather than conflict (#784 D37): sneshd is exactMatch, and every key covering the whole SNES is broadMatch over it — ES-DE's snes too, though asked, because the other pair narrows it (D36).

vectors.name: a-second-pair-narrows-a-romm-slug-to-one-system
vectors.rationale: RomM's genesis covers ES-DE's genesis, megadrive and megadrivejp; the bare folder megadrivejp names the Japanese Mega Drive alone, so the intersection is that one system (#784 D9, D14): ES-DE's, RetroDECK's and EmuDeck's megadrivejp exactMatch, and the keys that cover more broadMatch — RomM's genesis too, though asked, because the folder narrows it (D36).

vectors.name: an-overlap-key-beside-the-whole-system-leaves-the-system-broad
vectors.rationale: ROCKNIX's pc is related to ES-DE's dos: each covers something the other does not. Asked together, what they share is the part of dos that pc covers, so the asked dos is broadMatch to it, while pc, the key whose part it is, stays exactMatch (#784 D36).

vectors.name: one-engine-folder-is-one-part-in-every-distribution
vectors.rationale: Batocera and KNULLI both spell a gzdoom folder (batocera es_systems.yml:4623, knulli es_systems.yml:4556), one row a reviewed override declares a content subset of ES-DE's doom (#784 D37). Asked together they mean that one part: the intersection is agreed, both gzdoom keys are exactMatch, doom is broadMatch, prboom — the other engine subset of doom — is relatedMatch, and no caveat is stated.

vectors.name: a-key-on-a-row-and-its-subsets-meets-one-subset-inside-the-row
vectors.rationale: RomM's doom slug is placed on ES-DE's doom row whole and on Batocera's gzdoom and prboom rows, which a reviewed override declares content subsets of doom (romm platform_aliases.py:65 and :112, #784 D37). A key covering a row whole already holds that row's subsets, so asked beside batocera/gzdoom the two pairs share the gzdoom part inside doom: the intersection is agreed and states no caveat, gzdoom is exactMatch, prboom — the other engine subset of doom — is relatedMatch, and doom is broadMatch.

vectors.name: a-key-on-a-row-and-its-subsets-meets-one-subset-asked-first
vectors.rationale: The two pairs of the vector before, asked in the other order, answer the same intersection: agreed with no caveat, gzdoom exactMatch, prboom relatedMatch and doom broadMatch.

vectors.name: two-part-keys-of-one-system-share-it-unestablished
vectors.rationale: Batocera's gzdoom and prboom folders are rows a reviewed override declares content subsets of ES-DE's doom: each engine runs only part of the Doom games (#784 D37). Asked together they share doom only through two different parts of it, and the table cannot know whether those parts share content: the intersection is agreed on doom, both keys are relatedMatch to it, and platform-parts-unestablished names both pairs (#784 D40).

vectors.name: two-overlapping-romsets-share-the-arcade-unestablished
vectors.rationale: libretro's MAME and MAME 2000 are two romsets that each overlap the arcade systems rather than cover them. Asked together they share the arcade rows only through two overlaps, and the table cannot know whether those share content: the intersection is agreed, both keys are relatedMatch, and platform-parts-unestablished names both pairs (#784 D40, changed).
